why.reason: When the crowd is capitulating (bottom 20% price move) and fear is rising (bottom 15% F&G change), retail trapped longs are forced to sell into a volume vacuum, creating a mean-reversion snapback as smart money accumulates.

A weakness in the EMA gap combined with top traders reducing their net long exposure (bottom 33% position ratio) signals that smart money is de-risking or shorting, leading to a continued downtrend or deep dip before stabilization.

New stablecoin inflows (top 20%) provide dry powder while price drops (bottom 20%), and the divergence metric confirms that retail is selling while smart money is buying the dip, indicating institutional accumulation.

This team rule catches two distinct entry points: US buyers paying a premium during bullish momentum (Rule A) and a mean-reversion fade when ETH options fear is high but RSI is oversold (Rule B), diversifying entry triggers for the same 'smart money accumulation' theme.

merges.why: Rule #372 (Price/Fear bottom) and Rule #444 (EMA/TopTrader bottom) both signal 'smart money buying weakness', but #372 relies on retail sentiment while #444 relies on institutional positioning. An AND-merge ensures we only trade when BOTH retail capitulation AND institutional de-risking/accumulation

Rule #232 (Stablecoin inflow + Crowd/Smart divergence) uses a complex invented metric. Merging it with Rule #372's simple fear/price condition via UNION (OR) creates a robust 'Accumulation Team' that fires when EITHER new money is flowing in with smart-money divergence OR pure retail capitulation oc

pace.what: Fluid pace: several trades a day when the evidence is there (learned from its own opportunity rate), Grade S always allowed

guard.what: Risk guard: no second bet on the same move (correlation), total open risk capped by tail loss, daily and weekly brakes

kelly.what: Edge-proportional sizing: fractional Kelly from the calibrated odds (bigger only when the edge is proven)

online-fast.what: Learns which evidence is right from every scored candidate, forgets old evidence fast (Kalman-style online learning)

online-slow.what: Same online learning, forgets slowly (more stable)

without-positioning.what: Subtraction test: the referee without the 'positioning' witness (if it is no worse, 'positioning' is noise and goes)

without-flow.what: Subtraction test: the referee without the 'flow' witness (if it is no worse, 'flow' is noise and goes)

without-trend.what: Subtraction test: the referee without the 'trend' witness (if it is no worse, 'trend' is noise and goes)

without-volatility.what: Subtraction test: the referee without the 'volatility' witness (if it is no worse, 'volatility' is noise and goes)

without-leverage.what: Subtraction test: the referee without the 'leverage' witness (if it is no worse, 'leverage' is noise and goes)

without-realmoney.what: Subtraction test: the referee without the 'realmoney' witness (if it is no worse, 'realmoney' is noise and goes)

without-mood.what: Subtraction test: the referee without the 'mood' witness (if it is no worse, 'mood' is noise and goes)

without-invented.what: Subtraction test: the referee without the 'invented' witness (if it is no worse, 'invented' is noise and goes)

without-similar.what: Subtraction test: the referee without the 'similar' witness (if it is no worse, 'similar' is noise and goes)

doubt.what: Split jury: when the witnesses disagree with each other, the bar rises by how much they disagree

cointrust.what: Coin trust: demands more evidence on groups of coins where its own live odds proved too optimistic

rules.what: Research rules as fair witnesses: a rule counts only by its LIVE record in the current market state (trusted: odds up; keeps failing: a warning sign, odds down)

alloc.what: Daily-goal allocator: one budget per opportunity (up to 30% margin, 6% risk), all-in on one strong setup or split across 2-4 coins that are NOT the same bet; judged on account growth

lock.what: Profit lock: once a trade is well on its way the stop goes to break-even, and after the first target it always keeps at least half of the best open profit

curious.what: Curious: unfamiliar situations are grouped by kind; a kind with a proven live record becomes tradable (its own witness)

lowbar.what: Less cautious: half the safety margin above break-even (catches over-caution live)

pairs.what: Pair trades: long the coin it likes most, short the one it dislikes most, among coins that move together (the market's swings cancel; tight stop even in wild markets)

closed.why: long BNB (50%) vs short DOT (64%), coins that move together
long BNB (47%) vs short DOT (68%), coins that move together
long SEI (57%) vs short HBAR (69%), coins that move together

pairs.why: long XRP (57%) vs short FIL (68%), coins that move together

news.what: News drift: after a sudden market-wide shock, ride the move in its direction on the coin whose evidence agrees most (24h limit)

range.what: Range trades: in wild but sideways markets, short near the top of a coin's 3-day range and buy near the bottom (+1% target, stop just outside)

closed.why: range trade at the edge of its 3-day range

trend2.what: Compass trend reader: market direction from many views that must agree (Bitcoin's 20/50/200-day trends, breadth across coins, stocks, the dollar), five states incl. sideways, smoothed so noise cannot flip it

runner.what: Runner: on long signals, a small first risk, then one more unit at every further +2% with the stop one step behind, held up to 14 days (rare, very large winners; most attempts lose the first risk)

closed.why: runner: pyramids into a long that keeps going (+2% steps)

runs.why: runner: pyramids into a long that keeps going (+2% steps)

witness-macro.what: Outside-world witness: Nasdaq, S&P 500, VIX, US yields and the dollar (risk-on / risk-off), known only from the next day

gate.what: Trend gate: no shorts while the Compass trend reader says the market is rising. Over 7 past periods: +3.4% a month on average vs +2.0% without it, and the worst period improved from -11.9% to -2.0% a month

witness-onchain.what: On-chain witness: Bitcoin and Ethereum flowing into / out of exchanges, and exchange balances

witness-sectors.what: Sector witness: money rotating between AI, memes, layer-1s, DeFi and exchange tokens

witness-global.what: Compass global-markets witness: US, European and Asian stocks, the dollar, gold, oil, NVIDIA and chips, Coinbase, and how tightly Bitcoin follows stocks right now

witness-mood.what: Compass mood witness: the crypto Fear & Greed index and the options market's fear gauge (implied volatility), and how fast they are changing

witness-shock.what: Shock witness: how unusual the market's last moves were (what usually follows a shock like this)

bestofday.what: Best case of the day: the bar eases gradually through the day (to half its safety margin by the last hour) when nothing better has appeared

timestop.what: Time stop: a trade that has made no progress (under +0.5%) after 24 hours is closed instead of waiting for its stop

weekpace.what: Weekly pace with carry-over: a quiet day's unused trade can be used later in the same week (up to 3 in one day)

witness-flows.what: Compass money-flow witness: dollar stablecoin supply growing or shrinking (new money arriving in / leaving crypto)

witness-liq.what: Liquidation witness: how many longs and shorts were forcibly closed yesterday and over the last week, per coin and market-wide (Binance, Bybit and OKX, history since 2020)

recal.what: Recalibrated odds: the raw odds are corrected by what really happened to past candidates at each odds level (learned from the live ledger; no correction until 20 separate market moves are scored)

tiers.what: Conviction tiers: a small probe (0.5% risk) when the edge is thin, standard (1-2%) with 3+ points of edge and 2 witnesses, high conviction (3-4%) with 8+ points, 3 witnesses and the market state on its side

bold.what: Bold: the same trades as the Arbiter at double the risk (8% of the account at the stop for Grade A, 4% for Grade B)

witness-book.what: Order-book witness: how much money has been waiting to buy versus to sell near the price over the last days, and whether the book is getting thinner (Binance's own archive since 2023, one day behind)

bocpd-gate.what: Changepoint fast-track: Bayesian online changepoint detection on Bitcoin's return and market breadth; when a change is detected and the long side's graded calls since then beat their break-even over 15+ calls, longs unlock at once instead of waiting for the slow exam window

macro.what: Outside-world witness: Nasdaq, S&P 500, VIX, US yields and the dollar (risk-on / risk-off), known only from the next day

onchain.what: On-chain witness: Bitcoin and Ethereum flowing into / out of exchanges, and exchange balances

sectors.what: Sector witness: money rotating between AI, memes, layer-1s, DeFi and exchange tokens

global.what: Compass global-markets witness: US, European and Asian stocks, the dollar, gold, oil, NVIDIA and chips, Coinbase, and how tightly Bitcoin follows stocks right now

mood.what: Compass mood witness: the crypto Fear & Greed index and the options market's fear gauge (implied volatility), and how fast they are changing

flows.what: Compass money-flow witness: dollar stablecoin supply growing or shrinking (new money arriving in / leaving crypto)

book.what: Order-book witness: how much money has been waiting to buy versus to sell near the price over the last days, and whether the book is getting thinner (Binance's own archive since 2023, one day behind)

liq.what: Liquidation witness: how many longs and shorts were forcibly closed yesterday and over the last week, per coin and market-wide (Binance, Bybit and OKX, history since 2020)

shock.what: Shock witness: how unusual the market's last moves were (what usually follows a shock like this)

recorder.what: Recorder witness: liquidations, order-book and order-flow imbalance, live funding (own server)

Retail capitulation in crypto contrasts with emerging institutional interest, creating high volatility for digital assets.
